subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the exact first-frame composition of [Shot 1], showing the protagonist riding through the surveillance city with her companion robot, cyber motorcycle, giant red sun, exposed-concrete megastructures, stacked containers, white surveillance cameras, and digital-eye screens.

<Subject 1> is the same young dark-skinned female protagonist defined by <Picture 2> and <Picture 1>. Preserve her exact facial identity, skin tone, asymmetrical white dreadlocks, shaved sides, cyan-and-magenta face markings, magenta scarf, ivory technical outfit, tan cargo trousers, athletic body proportions, and single mechanical arm. <Picture 2> has the highest priority for her identity and mechanical-arm side.

<Subject 2> is the same compact flying companion robot defined by <Picture 3> and <Picture 1>. Preserve its rounded off-white body, magenta armor panels, single cyan optical eye, exactly two ducted-fan pods, two small manipulator arms, materials, proportions, and compact scale.

<Subject 3> is the exact rugged cyber motorcycle defined by <Picture 4> and <Picture 1>. <Picture 4> has the highest priority for its appearance and structure. Preserve its wheelbase, two knobby spoked wheels, cyan wheel accents, ivory-and-magenta armor, translucent magenta windscreen, twin cyan headlights, cyan front forks, black saddle, magenta frame, exposed metallic engine, rear suspension, and exactly two parallel exhaust silencers mounted together on the same rear-left side. Use one unchanged motorcycle throughout the video. Preserve the clean “079” side-panel region; if the digits cannot remain accurate, keep the panel clean instead of generating altered text.

<Subject 4> is the elevated surveillance-city environment defined by <Picture 5> and <Picture 1>. Preserve the narrow central road, stacked shipping containers, exposed-concrete cores, maintenance pipes, structural bridges, white cameras, repeated digital-eye screens, clouds beneath the city, giant calm red sun, and bright oppressive daylight.

<Audio 1> is the 15-second soundtrack reference. Its energy curve, electronic texture, transient accents, rhythmic changes, brief reductions in intensity, impact timing, and final cutoff guide the generated soundtrack and visual edit timing without directly copying the original signal.

summary:
[keyframe completion + reference generation + audio reference] The target is a 15-second, 16:9 cinematic 3D animated action sequence beginning exactly from <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> rides <Subject 3> through <Subject 4> while <Subject 2> flies beside her. The surveillance system locks onto them, the robot creates a brief interference window, and the motorcycle leaps across a cloud-filled gap before disappearing into a narrow concrete passage. One digital eye reactivates at the end. No reference video is used; all movement, camera motion and editing are defined by the written timeline and synchronized to <Audio 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the opening composition, subject placement, road perspective, lighting direction, red sun and surveillance-city atmosphere are preserved at 0.00 seconds.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the same face, skin tone, hairstyle, markings, costume, proportions and mechanical-arm side remain consistent.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the same single-eye robot, two fan pods, two manipulator arms, colors and compact scale remain consistent.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the exact motorcycle from <Picture 4> remains unchanged, including its proportions, wheels, armor, windscreen, frame, engine, suspension, color blocking and dual-exhaust configuration.
<Subject 4> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the same construction system, red sun, high-altitude clouds, surveillance devices, color palette and daylight remain continuous.
<Audio 1>: reference - its rhythm, energy changes, electronic texture, transient accents and final cutoff guide the generated audio and edit timing without copying the source signal.

detailed_description:
The target video uses premium stylized cinematic 3D animation with physically based materials, restrained graphic edge treatment, bright permanent daylight, warm coral highlights, cool cyan sky fill, deep neutral shadows and thin high-altitude haze. The city appears beautiful and fashionable at first glance but mechanically cold and oppressive. No reference video is used. All character movement, vehicle motion, robot flight, camera movement and cuts follow the instructions below.

[Shot 1] The video begins exactly from <Picture 1>. A low front three-quarter tracking shot moves backward at fast speed ahead of <Subject 3> as <Subject 1> rides toward the camera through <Subject 4>. She lowers her chest over the motorcycle, keeps both hands naturally gripping the handlebars and looks forward with a focused, defiant expression. Her white dreadlocks and magenta scarf stream backward under the airflow while her mechanical arm remains correctly connected and anatomically stable.

<Subject 2> flies close to her right-rear side, matching her speed through small synchronized corrections from its two ducted fans. Identical white cameras rotate toward her in a sequential wave. Digital-eye screens illuminate from foreground to background, their irises tightening as they acquire the target. The opening visual movement and camera acceleration synchronize with the first transient rise in <Audio 1>. The camera remains smooth and controlled while the container walls receive restrained horizontal motion blur.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.500, a narrow horizontal glitch tear creates a hard cut synchronized with a rhythmic change in <Audio 1>. The camera switches to a lateral tracking shot. <Subject 2> rises slightly and emits one short cyan interference pulse along the surveillance-screen array. The pulse affects only the screens and camera lenses; it does not distort the protagonist, robot, motorcycle or architecture.

The digital eyes break into controlled horizontal static, and several cameras freeze mid-turn. <Subject 1> twists the throttle, shifts her weight forward and accelerates <Subject 3> toward the rising ramp. The suspension compresses naturally over the uneven road while both wheels remain aligned and connected to the surface. The windscreen, armor, frame, engine, two wheels and exactly two rear-left exhaust silencers remain identical to <Picture 4>. The camera whip-pans right with large amplitude at fast speed, then stabilizes beside the motorcycle as it climbs the ramp.

[Shot 3] At 00:09.500, the camera cuts to a wide side view as <Subject 3> launches from the platform into open air above the clouds. The change to the airborne shot synchronizes with the brief reduction in intensity within <Audio 1>. The giant red sun remains calm behind <Subject 1>, creating a clear silhouette while preserving her face, hairstyle, costume and mechanical-arm identity.

<Subject 2> follows the same flight arc slightly above and behind the motorcycle. The camera tracks them at fast speed with large amplitude while the container towers and concrete bridges slide across the background. The motorcycle remains structurally rigid in flight: both wheels stay circular and aligned, the frame does not bend, the fairings do not change, and no components detach or transform.

At approximately 00:12.600, <Subject 3> lands hard on the opposite platform in synchronization with the strongest late impact in <Audio 1>. The front and rear suspension compress once and recover naturally. <Subject 1> steadies the motorcycle and accelerates into a narrow concrete passage.

At 00:14.300, the camera performs a sudden short zoom toward one foreground digital-eye screen. The static clears, its iris reopens, and a final horizontal glitch tear freezes the image at 00:15.000, synchronized with the final electronic cutoff of <Audio 1>.

Across all shots, preserve the same woman, mechanical-arm side, robot, motorcycle and city. Do not mirror the protagonist, change her face, duplicate the robot, add fan pods, alter the motorcycle model, change its wheelbase, add wheels, remove or duplicate exhausts, bend the frame, detach components, deform hands, fuse subjects, change colors, generate random decals, produce false numbers, add text, introduce excessive neon, use cheap cyan bloom, shift into nighttime cyberpunk imagery, or imitate visual details from any unlisted video source.

overall_soundscape:
The generated physical sound follows <Audio 1> as a reference for timing and texture without copying it directly. Strong high-altitude wind continues beneath the motorcycle’s rising engine tone, tire friction, suspension impacts, the robot’s compact ducted-fan whine and synchronized camera-servo rotations. A short electrical crackle accompanies the interference pulse, followed by a heavy landing impact, brief tire skid and one clean electronic activation tone when the final eye reopens.

non_diegetic_music:
The generated score references <Audio 1> for its electronic timbre, rhythmic density, transient positions, brief airborne reduction and final cutoff without directly reusing the source signal. Use a fast hybrid electronic breakbeat with tight industrial percussion, low distorted synth pulses and sparse metallic impacts. The rhythm briefly thins during the jump, returns with one heavy bass accent on landing and ends with an abrupt digital cutoff.
